ns2:section.sectionText: This is a hands-on (learn-by-doing) practical course in elicitation of linguistic data, and theoretical analysis of that data, from an unfamiliar language. Students will elicit, record, and transcribe data collected in group interviews. The class as a whole will work on a language archive: (i) recordings collected throughout the semester and their transcriptions, (ii) a dictionary with vocabulary translated into English, (iii) the final projects. This course provides advanced undergraduate students with the opportunity to integrate their previous training with this practical experience and the class will depend on the experience they have up to date with phonology, phonetics, morphology, syntax, semantics. Prerequisites: LING 301, LING 302, and one of the following courses: LING 304 or LING 307.
